premise: Plot: N313's infiltration and destruction of TX-55. Story: the rookie Snake learns to judge authority, protect others, and form earned relationships with veterans and resistance. The game should satisfy both.
doctrine: Every story beat is tied to a physical room, mission event, returning encounter, character choice, optional codec or authored film shot. No characters telepathically know an event. No unearned twist/early retcon. Never claim invented lines are authentic 1987 transcription.

characters.canonical: FOXHOUND rookie Solid Snake; infiltrates Outer Heaven, rescues Gray Fox, uncovers and defeats Metal Gear and Big Boss.
characters.wants: complete N313 and prove he belongs among veterans
characters.needs: learn that loyalty requires independently verifying orders and protecting people, not just satisfying command
characters.wound: fear of failing his first real assignment; loneliness behind disciplined wit
characters.performance: restrained, observant, increasingly willing to ask difficult questions; short lines and expressive pauses, no clairvoyant exposition
characters.firstPayoff: Snake chooses to listen to Fox beyond the mandatory nuclear-weapon clue
characters.finalPayoff: Snake confronts the commander he once relied on, preserving the 1987 identity reveal timing

characters.canonical: Snake's commander, ultimately revealed as Outer Heaven's leader in original story
characters.wants: maintain control of Snake's mission and the fortress narrative
characters.needs: never telegraph secret identity through inexplicably evil early dialogue; retain believable mentor persona
characters.wound: his personal motives are later-series context, not original 1987 in-scene proof
characters.performance: capable, concise, sometimes warmly protective, later evasive only when Snake earns contradictory evidence
characters.finalPayoff: final betrayal lands as the rupture of an established relationship

characters.canonical: veteran FOXHOUND operative held in Outer Heaven; knows Metal Gear's nature
characters.wants: survive detention long enough to put his intel in another soldier's hands
characters.needs: be a person whose competence survives captivity, not a key-bearing lore dispenser
characters.wound: isolation, exhaustion and the experience of counting unseen guard changes
characters.performance: economical, exhausted but sharp and protective; recognition and listening before revelations
characters.firstPayoff: optional shift-pattern conversation opens a low-risk player advantage
characters.finalPayoff: his warning affects how Snake weighs later orders without granting future secrets

characters.canonical: local resistance leader/former Outer Heaven architect; architectural assistance over radio
characters.wants: help dismantle a fortress whose architecture was exploited
characters.needs: show real limits to his knowledge; changed plans and sealed tunnels require investigation
characters.wound: responsibility for a place later turned against civilians
characters.performance: precise technical terminology, emotional restraint, confidence limited to corridors he built
characters.firstPayoff: describes a real repaired seam or service duct Snake can inspect
characters.finalPayoff: revisit commentary turns his remorse into useful work, not guilt monologues

characters.canonical: resistance intelligence source supplying information on enemies and bosses
characters.wants: keep resistance cells alive by being useful without being exposed
characters.needs: recognised as an experienced observer, not a button that tells the boss weakness
characters.wound: the limitations of secondhand reports and late contact
characters.performance: direct, dry, bold; revises assessments after the player reports contradictory evidence
characters.firstPayoff: boss analysis only after frequency earned and encounter witnessed

characters.canonical: resistance member embedded in Outer Heaven medical staff, searching for missing brother
characters.wants: find brother and keep detainees alive
characters.needs: player must earn trust and access rather than buy her as a vendor
characters.wound: cannot openly help without risking her cover
characters.performance: professional, urgent, personable under low-volume secrecy
characters.firstPayoff: medic supply help when Snake meets actual original rank/frequency gate
characters.finalPayoff: brother's fate/escape clue matters as a human relationship

characters.canonical: Dr. Pettrovich, engineer coerced to develop TX-55 with daughter held hostage
characters.wants: save Ellen without triggering her captors
characters.needs: engineer's shame and practical intelligence must be causally connected
characters.performance: precise technical language interrupted by concern for Ellen
characters.firstPayoff: will not give unearned final sabotage steps
characters.finalPayoff: after Ellen's rescue, technical help becomes an act of repair

characters.canonical: daughter held hostage to coerce Dr. Pettrovich
characters.wants: get out and have her father survive
characters.needs: moment of agency and a life beyond a quest-marker
characters.wound: she knows the facility through captivity but not future secret facts
characters.performance: subtle, pragmatic, points Snake to a real return route rather than a world map
characters.firstPayoff: her safe rescue changes the father's motivation and dialogue
characters.finalPayoff: Snake understands which civilians his mission actually protected

characters.canonical: hostages/prisoners grant rank and world information in original game
characters.wants: survival and hope that the outside world remembers them
characters.needs: not anonymous vending machines for frequency/keycards
characters.performance: short individual identities, credible knowledge constrained by where held
characters.firstPayoff: Snake's first rescue changes his priorities before rank rewards
characters.finalPayoff: last prisoner reveal is earned, not spoiled through early dialogue
